judged_text: Stored XSS on the feed path: TopicEmbed.import stores third-party feed content with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw verbatim) and it is served as cooked HTML with no sanitization — poll_feed.rb uses CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) with zero tag/attribute filtering (not even the readability whitelist used in import_remote), and unescapeHTML actively re-decodes entity-encoded payloads; embed/best.html.erb renders raw post.cooked (and normal topic pages render it too), so any script/iframe tag in the configured feed becomes stored XSS executing on the Discourse origin — the feed path needs the same tag/attribute whitelist applied in import_remote

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a path where untrusted third‑party HTML is persisted and later rendered without sanitization. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` parses the feed and passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly into `TopicEmbed.import` (no tag/attribute filtering), while `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` short-circuits the cooking/sanitization pipeline by returning `raw` verbatim. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` (and the model spec asserts `post.cooked == post.raw` for these imports), making stored XSS via feed content verifiable from the diff.
